newsitem.title: USA: BioTransplant Xenomune on patent allowance.
newsitem.headline: BioTransplant Xenomune on patent allowance.

text.p: BioTransplant Inc said that an allowance has been issued by the United States Patent and Trademark Office for a patent application involving the company's proprietary XenoMune transplantation system.

The regulatory agency's action was announced by Elliott Lebowitz, BioTransplant's president and chief executive officer, who spoke Tuesday at a life sciences conference in London conducted by UBS Securities, the company said.
BioTransplant's XenoMune system seeks to establish tolerance in transplants to allow acceptance of pigs' organs while maintaining the recipient's immune system, the company said.
The grant of a patent allowance is the last step before an actual patent is granted, according to BioTransplant spokeswoman Gretchen Scheweitzer.

Bio-Transplant said that transplant tolerance could be achieved through inactivation of components of the recipient's immune system, followed by the grafting of the thymus from a fetal swine to rebuild the recipient's immune system.
Co-inventors on the patent, which is exclusively licensed to BioTransplant, are Megan Sykes, and David Sachs, both physicians at the the Massachusetts General Hospital, the company said.
